sources.title: Value Added Tax Return, form CT 205 (Value Added Tax Act [Cap 247]): sixteen numbered boxes — 5 to 10 the VAT on sales and income (box 5 total sales including VAT, box 6 zero-rated supplies, box 7 = box 5 less box 6, box 8 = box 7 divided by 7.6667, box 9 adjustments, box 10 = boxes 8 and 9), 11 to 15 the VAT on purchases and expenses (box 11 purchases including VAT but without imports, box 12 = box 11 divided by 7.6667, box 13 VAT paid to Customs on imported goods, box 14 adjustments, box 15 = boxes 12, 13 and 14) and box 16 the difference between boxes 10 and 15 (refund or VAT to pay); the pay-in slip carries boxes 17 to 19
sources.publisher: Government of Vanuatu — Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR)

sources.title: Value added tax — introduction: VAT at 15 % on most goods and services, registration above VT 4 million of taxable supplies in 12 months (voluntary below), exempt supplies (financial services, residential rental, education, donated goods of a non-profit body) and zero-rated supplies (exports), monthly return or quarterly below VT 8 million, due the 27th of the following month

sources.title: Change of VAT rate to 15 per cent — the Parliament raised the rate from 12.5 % to 15 % from 1 January 2018; VAT-inclusive prices divide by 7.6667 (3/23) to find the VAT, VAT-exclusive prices multiply by 3/20

charts.name: Vanuatu reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Vanuatu, and no text read names a standard setter or a framework for company accounts. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-style statements below (IAS 1, expenses by nature), with the accounts a Vanuatu trading company keeps — VAT output and input tax, import VAT owed to Customs at the border, and the liabilities for withholding and contributions.

numbering.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act [Cap. 247], s. 21 — a registered person making a taxable supply to another registered person provides a tax invoice within 28 days of a request, with the particulars of the approved form; a buyer-created tax invoice needs the Director's approval and the words “buyer created tax invoice – VAT approved”. The text read states no document numbering rule, so numbering is `free`; the number format is a convention of this pack.

tax_point.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act [Cap. 247], s. 5(1) — a supply takes place at the earliest of the time an invoice is issued and the time a payment is received; s. 17 lets the registered person account for the tax on an invoice basis or on a payments basis, and a person who elects nothing is deemed to be on the payments basis. `invoice_if_issued` states the invoice as the point of the tax where one is issued, the invoice basis; the payments basis and a payment received before the invoice are gaps recorded in the README.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No structured e-invoice standard, Peppol profile or clearance system of the Department was found in the texts read; the VAT return is lodged at the counter, by post or by e-mail. `obligation` is `none` for want of a text, not on a finding that none exists.

not_taxed.legal_reference: The texts read (Value Added Tax Act [Cap. 247] in its 2020 consolidation, form CT 205 and the Department's brochures) name no reverse charge on services bought from abroad: the form has no box for it and the Act's place-of-supply rule (s. 7) was not read to a conclusion. The pack therefore carries no purchase tax for them. This is a finding about the texts read, not a finding that no such rule exists: it is a gap recorded in the README.
